trim_recommendations.rationale: Section 2.5 (Deep Learning for Volatility Forecasting) is a 5-line stub. The paper does NOT present any LSTM/GRU as a main contribution; the deep learning models appear only as null results in Section 4.7. The literature review subsection adds nothing to the narrative arc. The LSTM/GRU null result is already explained briefly in Section 4.7 without needing its own lit-review setup.
trim_recommendations.content_loss: Minimal — no main results rely on this subsection. The citation to Kim & Kim (2019) and Bucci (2020) can be dropped or folded into a parenthetical in Sec 4.7.

trim_recommendations.section: Section 4.6 – Robustness Checks: Window Size Subsection (§4.6.1)
trim_recommendations.action: CONDENSE from ~1 dense page to ~0.4 pages
trim_recommendations.rationale: Subsection 4.6.1 (Window Size and Proxy Sensitivity) is extremely dense — it covers the U-shape QLIKE analysis, cross-OOS validation across 6 windows, crisis performance, MaxDD tradeoffs, computation cost, rebalancing interaction, AND cross-asset confirmation all in one paragraph. Much of this detail (especially the w=378 optimum, rebalancing interaction, the specific Sharpe numbers 0.70/1.06/0.37) duplicates or extends material from Table 7 (Window Size table). The key message — 'gamma sign classification is window-invariant; w=504 recommended' — can be stated in 3-4 sentences with a pointer to Table 7. The U-shape elaboration, cross-asset breakdown, and computation time note should be cut.
trim_recommendations.content_loss: Detail about w=378 optimum and rebalancing×window interaction — these are peripheral robustness points, not core claims.

trim_recommendations.rationale: The df robustness discussion (df ∈ {4, 4.5, 5, ..., 10}) repeats information already stated in Section 3.4.3 VaR Backtesting (lines 120-125) where the fixed df=5 choice is already justified. The second paragraph about rolling df estimation repeats what is presented more concisely elsewhere. The key conclusion (fixed df≤6 beats estimated df) can be stated in 2 sentences here, pointing back to Section 3.4.3.
trim_recommendations.content_loss: Specific numbers for each tested df value — already summarized in Table 4b reference.

trim_recommendations.rationale: This section (Henriksson-Merton, Treynor-Mazuy, Merton timing ratio) presents three tests that all return the same null result: VT has no directional timing ability. The three equations + individual results paragraphs are repetitive. The core message is a single finding: 'All three timing tests confirm no directional timing (p>0.70); VT operates through variance management not return prediction.' This can be compressed to a single paragraph with inline results. The regime decomposition paragraph at the end duplicates the VT insurance discussion (§5.4/5.6). Additionally, this material largely overlaps with §5.4 'Nature of VT Alpha' which also reports the Henriksson-Merton alpha and negative γ_HM — there is substantial verbatim repetition.
trim_recommendations.content_loss: Individual paragraphs for each timing test, the full equations (these are standard refs), and the regime decomposition which is covered in §5.4.

trim_recommendations.action: MERGE into Section 4.2.4 (Robustness) as a short paragraph, DELETE as standalone Discussion subsection
trim_recommendations.rationale: §5.2 is only ~3 sentences (a single paragraph). It reports that SPY's ETF-level γ is 2.7× larger than its constituent average. This is a minor supporting finding that does not warrant its own Discussion subsection. It could be absorbed as a 2-sentence note within §4.2.4 Robustness or §4.2.2 Economic Interpretation. Removing a standalone subsection header also improves flow.
trim_recommendations.content_loss: None — content moves to a more appropriate location.

trim_recommendations.action: MERGE into Section 4.2.5 (Regime-Dependent Leverage in Gold)
trim_recommendations.rationale: §5.3 discusses the regression of rolling gamma on volatility regime AND the post-2022 SPY-TLT correlation change. The γ-on-volatility regression (slope=-0.36, R²=0.07) is directly related to the regime-dependent leverage finding already established in §4.2.5 — it belongs there as a quantitative refinement. The SPY-TLT correlation finding (the 60/40 portfolio concern) is genuinely interesting but only one sentence — it would fit naturally as a note in §5.4 on practical portfolio implications. Removing as a standalone section saves the subsection header overhead and avoids Discussion fragmentation.
trim_recommendations.content_loss: None — content moves to more integrated locations.

trim_recommendations.rationale: Appendix C is a ~0.7-page implementation bullet-point summary. At the Journal of Banking and Finance level, implementation summaries of this type are typically inappropriate — they read more like a practitioner note. The information is already covered in the body (§3.2 for model specification, §3.4.3 for df=5, §5.8 for 12/VIX implementation). A JBF editor would likely ask this to be cut or converted to a footnote. If retained, it should be folded into the Conclusion paragraph on practical implications.
trim_recommendations.content_loss: Marginal — all technical details are already in the main text.

trim_recommendations.rationale: §5.7 currently covers international equities (10 markets), currency carry (AUD/JPY), and commodities in exhaustive detail. The AUD/JPY carry discussion (Sharpe 0.146→0.426, a 70/30 portfolio achieving Sharpe 0.898) is peripheral to the paper's core contributions about leverage direction and model selection — it reads like a separate paper. The VIX-correlation threshold (ρ>0.60 empirical rule) is the main takeaway and should be stated directly. The 10-market international equity analysis can be summarized in 2-3 sentences. Detailed carry trade performance numbers should be trimmed to 1 sentence.
trim_recommendations.content_loss: Detailed carry trade statistics and the 70/30 diversification result — these are interesting but peripheral to the core thesis.

trim_recommendations.action: CONDENSE the VIX sufficient statistic mega-paragraph (lines 583-586)
trim_recommendations.rationale: The VIX sufficient statistic test results paragraph (lines 583-586) is extremely dense — it covers 16 categories of indicators, 5 sub-categories, Taiwan exception, causal PC algorithm analysis, all in one paragraph. This creates readability problems and risks losing the reader. The key results (all 42 FRED series, partial r<0.03; Taiwan import YoY the only exception; causal PC confirms VIX as information sink) can be stated in 4-5 sentences rather than 6+ dense lines. The causal discovery (PC algorithm, in-degree=4, out-degree=1) is a nice finding but the paragraph-long explanation can be cut to 2 sentences.
trim_recommendations.content_loss: Detail on specific macro variable subcategories — the table already captures this.

trim_recommendations.section: Section 4.10 – Real-Time Crisis Validation: 2026 Iran Episode
trim_recommendations.rationale: The Iran crisis section covers four sub-items (market impact, VaR, gamma direction, VT) in detail. The market impact paragraph has specifics (USO 73% YTD, 2.52× volatility increase) that are valuable. However, the VaR paragraph repeats the validation structure already established in §4.4; it could be condensed to 2 sentences noting all 6 assets achieved Green Zone. The Hybrid VT paragraph lists 10 crisis episodes with individual drawdown numbers — these could be presented in a table (or are already in Figure 4) rather than inline text. The switching threshold robustness (Sharpe in [0.93, 0.98]) can be cut to 1 sentence.
trim_recommendations.content_loss: Redundant restatement of VaR methodology applied to Iran data; detailed inline crisis episodes list.

trim_recommendations.rationale: This subsection covers EGARCH sign alignment, HAC correction, the 2019-2026 sample, and the 2013-2015 regime. Much of the 2013-2015 material is repeated almost verbatim in §4.2.5 (Regime-Dependent Leverage) — the 2005-2016 finding (52% negative), the bull/bear test (t=-4.71), and the economic interpretation all appear in BOTH subsections. After §4.2.5 is retained as a dedicated subsection (per constraints), §4.2.4 should just say 'sign classification is robust to window size and estimation period; see §4.2.5 for regime dependence' and drop the duplicated bear-market statistics.
trim_recommendations.content_loss: One duplicate paragraph already covered in §4.2.5.

trim_recommendations.section: Table T9 (tab:tail) – Tail Risk Metrics for Hybrid VT
trim_recommendations.rationale: Table T9 (7 tail risk metrics for SPY Hybrid VT vs. BH) is supplementary. The most important metrics (ES 1%, worst day, worst 5-day) are already mentioned in the text. This table is unlikely to be required by JBF reviewers as a main-text table — it would be fine in an appendix or online supplement. Moving it saves ~0.5p in the tables section.
trim_recommendations.content_loss: Minimal — the key numbers (ES 1% = -4.68% BH vs -1.35% VT, kurtosis reduction) can be cited inline.

trim_recommendations.section: Section 5.4 'The Nature of VT Alpha' subsubsection — HM alpha repetition
trim_recommendations.action: MERGE with §4.9 Formal Market Timing Tests
trim_recommendations.rationale: §5.4 'The Nature of VT Alpha' (lines 452-456) and §4.9 'Formal Market Timing Tests' (lines 383-403) both report the Henriksson-Merton test results for the Hybrid VT strategy. Both report the same α=5.77%, γ_HM=-0.043, t=-4.06. This is the most direct case of verbatim numerical repetition in the paper. The fix: fold all the HM/TM/TR test material from §4.9 into §5.4, and in §4.9 just say 'See Section 5.4 for market timing test results.' Or alternatively, keep §4.9 as the results section and cut §5.4's numerical repetition to a 1-line summary.

total_estimated_savings.note_on_doublespacing: Paper uses \doublespacing. Each prose paragraph cut translates to ~0.6-0.8 page savings per 10-12 lines. Table removal at single-spacing ~0.3-0.5pp each. Total above achieves ~7.1pp from content cuts; additional ~1-2pp likely from paragraph-level tight editing throughout (introduction, data section, conclusion). Confidence interval: 7-10pp total.

jbf_specific_guidance.word_limit: JBF has no formal page limit but referees typically expect ≤55pp for empirical papers with this scope. The current 64pp is at the outer boundary.
jbf_specific_guidance.biggest_jbf_risk: The paper has THREE appendices. JBF typically expects at most one. Appendix A (Commodity Extension) and Appendix C (Implementation Summary) are candidates for the online supplement.
jbf_specific_guidance.section_imbalance: Discussion (§5) is 18pp vs Results (§4) 22pp — this 18pp Discussion is unusually long for JBF. The cross-asset VT, VT insurance, and complexity ceiling subsections read like separate papers. T8 (cross-asset trim) directly addresses this.
jbf_specific_guidance.contribution_count: Abstract promises 2 contributions; Introduction §1 also lists 2 main + 1 time-zone contribution (Contribution 3 = TZ info transmission). The time-zone contribution is acknowledged as non-implementable and belongs in Appendix B. Consider whether it should remain a numbered 'Contribution' in the Introduction or be presented as 'additional evidence' to avoid inflating the paper's scope.
